::: {.question-card}
## Research question

Where should a manufacturing supply chain place its facilities, and how much on-site wind, solar and storage should each facility install when facilities can trade energy with the grid?
:::

::: {.proj-cards}
::: {.info-card .glow-card .ic-contribution}
## My contribution

First author of the location-allocation papers (AMM, SEGRE). Second author of the JORS paper, for which I built the optimization models and the case-study analyses.
:::

::: {.info-card .glow-card .ic-method}
## Method

JORS sizes on-site microgrids for fixed facility locations with production and inventory planning; AMM and SEGRE add facility location-allocation decisions.
:::

:::

## Key findings

::: {.findings}
1. Facility siting trades transport cost against renewable resource quality (AMM).
2. On-site renewables lower total supply-chain cost under the modeled time-of-use tariffs.
3. In the AMM price scenarios, batteries became attractive at high peak electricity prices; in JORS, capping grid imports made storage worthwhile.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Boundary conditions"}
Stylized multi-echelon networks with synthetic distances and costs.
:::

:::
